scenario.description: A 4/4 creature survives combat with 2 damage marked on it. No effect changes its toughness or the marked damage before the cleanup step.

question.prompt: When is that marked damage normally removed?

options.text: Immediately after combat.
At the beginning of the next upkeep.
During the cleanup step.
When the creature becomes tapped.

questions.explanation: Damage marked on permanents is removed during the cleanup step as part of a turn-based action. It is not removed immediately when combat ends.
questions.takeaway: Damage marked on permanents is removed during the cleanup step as part of a turn-based action.

questions.title: Sorcery timing

scenario.description: It is your opponent's turn. You have a sorcery card in hand and no effect grants permission to cast it at another time.

question.prompt: Can you cast the sorcery now?

options.text: Yes, if you have priority.
Yes, if the stack is empty.
No. A sorcery normally requires your own main phase, priority, and an empty stack.
Yes, during any combat step.

questions.explanation: A sorcery can normally be cast only when you have priority during a main phase of your own turn and the stack is empty. Having priority alone is not enough.
questions.takeaway: A sorcery can normally be cast only when you have priority during a main phase of your own turn and the stack is empty.
